title: Philosophy for kids: what is fair?
examples: Teacher, if everyone gets the same amount, is that always fair?
What makes a rule fair for everyone?
Can sharing things sometimes feel unfair?

explain.say: We are learning about what it means to be fair today.

draw.text: Philosophy for kids: what is fair?

items: Fairness is about what is right.
It is about treating people well.

explain.say: Sharing means giving things to other people.
Sometimes sharing things equally is not the same as being fair.
Rules help us know what is expected in a group.
If two friends are building a tower, a rule might be to take turns.
In real life, being fair means thinking about everyone's needs.

faq.q: If everyone gets the same number of stickers, is that always fair?
faq.a: No, it is not always fair. Fairness means giving what someone needs, not just the same amount.
asks: Does fairness mean giving different things?

faq.q: Why do we need rules when we play games?
faq.a: Rules help everyone know what to do so that the game is fun and fair for all players.
asks: What happens if we don't have rules?

faq.q: What if one person is much stronger than the others?
faq.a: Fairness means making sure the stronger person still has a chance to play and win.
asks: How do we make games fair for everyone?
Should rules change if someone is very good?

faq.q: Is it okay to make up a rule if it seems fair?
faq.a: Sometimes, groups need to agree on new rules together to make things fair for everyone.
asks: Can we make our own rules?
Who decides if a rule is fair?

faq.q: What is the difference between equal and fair?
faq.a: Equal means the same for everyone. Fair means what is right for each person in that situation.
asks: Are equal and fair the same thing?
When is 'the same' not good enough?

facts: Fairness is about justice and what is right.
Sharing can be equal or fair, depending on the situation.
Rules help groups make decisions and play together.
Sometimes, fairness means giving more help to someone who needs it more.

quiz.say: Three friends are coloring pictures. Friend A needs blue crayons, Friend B needs red crayons, and Friend C has enough of both.
quiz.show: Who gets the extra red crayons?

options.show: Give the friend who has the most crayons the extra red ones.
options.say: Give the friend who has the most crayons the extra red ones.

options.show: Give the friend who needs red crayons the extra red ones.
options.say: Give the friend who needs red crayons the extra red ones.

options.show: Give all three friends exactly five red crayons.
options.say: Give all three friends exactly five red crayons.

options.show: Take the extra red crayons and give them to the teacher.
options.say: Take the extra red crayons and give them to the teacher.

quiz.why: This is fair because Friend B needs the red crayons more than Friend C.

wrong.0: This is not fair because it ignores who actually needs the crayons right now.
wrong.2: This is equal, but it is not fair because Friend A does not need red crayons.
wrong.3: This is not fair because the friends still need the crayons for their pictures.

quiz.say: A group is deciding on a rule for recess playtime.

options.show: The rule should only be about the strongest players.
options.say: The rule should only be about the strongest players.

options.show: The rule should only be about the teacher's favourite game.
options.say: The rule should only be about the teacher's favourite game.

options.show: The rule should help everyone play safely.
options.say: The rule should help everyone play safely.

options.show: The rule should be the easiest rule to remember.
options.say: The rule should be the easiest rule to remember.

quiz.why: A good rule keeps everyone safe and makes sure the game is fun for all.

wrong.0: A rule must be fair for the weakest players too.
wrong.1: Fair rules must be agreed upon by the whole group.
wrong.3: While easy is nice, the rule must also keep everyone safe.

quiz.say: Your class is sharing new books. One student loves space books, another loves animal books, and a third loves history books.

options.show: Put all the books in the middle and let them fight for them.
options.say: Put all the books in the middle and let them fight for them.

options.show: Give each student a book about the topic they like best.
options.say: Give each student a book about the topic they like best.

options.show: Give every student one book about space.
options.say: Give every student one book about space.

options.show: Give the student who reads the fastest the best book.
options.say: Give the student who reads the fastest the best book.

quiz.why: This is fair because it meets the specific needs or interests of each person.

wrong.0: This is unsafe and not a fair way to share things.
wrong.2: This is equal, but the student who loves animals might feel left out.
wrong.3: This is not fair because reading speed does not show what a person likes.
